rv.q: Godinez’s “Measure for Measure” is a Shakespearean production with a heavy concept that works.
Godinez has shaved it down to its essence and made its Cuban setting both immensely vivid, specific and universal.
In all, this is one fascinating and enthralling version of Shakespeare, filled with contemporary ideas, that will certainly appeal to everyone.
Godinez masterfully paces this tight with layers of special touches.
Henry Godinez's streamlined (about 100 intermissionless minutes) and vibrant production at Chicago Shakespeare comes pretty damn close.
For those who are Shakespeare fans but aren't in the mood for one of his three hour dramas or history plays, this 100-minute Measure for Measure might be the one for you.
Overall, Godinez’s direction and Chicago Shakespeare’s vibrant staging make for a rewarding evening of theater.
Both Adam Poss and Cruz Gonzalez-Cadel gave more the impression of reading, and not quite convincingly at that.

cn.t: Critics praise Chicago Shakespeare's *Measure for Measure* as vibrant and immersive, with Henry Godinez's bold Havana-set production breathing fresh life into Shakespeare's problem play. The sexy 1950s Cuban atmosphere and streamlined staging earn widespread acclaim.
